verdictBasis: 0 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 4 advisories. ACCEPT was gated at 0 blockers AND 0 SHOULD-FIX.
verdictStatement: Every blocker from both v6 verdicts is closed, and closed properly rather than relabelled. linux-distro-userspace is now a versioned closed payload — schemeId opensip-linux-distro-userspace.1, two fields with named os-release(5) sources, per-field normalization that differs deliberately between them, a ten-entry knownIds vocabulary with a deterministic OTHER-PUBLISHER digest escape for everything outside it, a serialization naming its delimiter by code point, byte-exact equality, and an explicit normalizationReferent that resolves the dangling 'after normalization' clause I raised. The open platform-image alternate form is not softened but removed and denied twice. OTHER-FSTYPE now names one interface per osFamily, correctly identifies Linux mountinfo rather than the f_fstypename field that does not exist there, states that normalization precedes the enum lookup, and deletes the 'or equivalent' escape. sonameAbi is excluded from sameMeans and from drift in four separate places, with presence, absence and mismatch all named. The pin-rotation rule is stated as a standing rule and explicitly ties back to the honestyRepairsFromV4 line whose claim it supports. What holds acceptance is one element of PTCB-V6-B2's required repair that did not land: the filesystem observation still has no failure behaviour, and the rule selecting which mount record supplies the token is underspecified for the bind and overlay cases where more than one record can answer.

shouldFix.title: OTHER-FSTYPE names its per-osFamily sources but states no failure behaviour and no record-selection rule for the resolved volume

measurement.againstTheFrozenRequirement: PTCB-V6-B2's requiredRepair reads 'For each osFamily, name one exact observation API/field or a versioned mapping algorithm, including the filesystem/mount being measured and failure behavior. Remove the (or equivalent) escape, state that normalization occurs before enum lookup, and use OTHER-FSTYPE only when that normalized token is absent.' Five of its six elements are delivered. Failure behaviour is not stated anywhere for this member.
measurement.whatIsMissing: No rule covers an unobtainable token: no /proc/self/mountinfo record matching the resolved volume, /proc not mounted in the observing context, or an empty f_fstypename. emptyRejected: true stops an empty value from occupying the member and beforeAllowlistFreeze stops a freeze with an unpopulated member, so the artifact fails closed by implication — but implication is the standard this lineage has consistently rejected, and the artifact's own sibling repair states the analogous rule outright: userspaceRelease says 'If VERSION_ID is absent the profile refuses.'
measurement.recordSelection: The Linux source reads 'the /proc/self/mountinfo record whose mount point is the resolved volume'. That presumes the volume's mount point is already known. Determining it from a resolved object requires a longest-matching-prefix rule over mount points, which is not stated, and under bind mounts or overlay stacks more than one mountinfo record can carry the same mount point, so 'the record' is not uniquely determined. The macOS source does not have this problem: statfs is evaluated on the object itself.

shouldFix.consequence: Two conforming verifiers can select different mountinfo records for one resolved object on a bind-mounted or overlay filesystem, producing different OTHER-FSTYPE digests for the same host, or diverge between refusing and proceeding when the token cannot be observed. Fail-closed in both directions rather than exploitable, but the required member is not yet reproducible for those cases.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Add a failure clause matching the userspaceRelease one — if the token cannot be observed from the named interface the profile refuses — and state the record-selection rule: the mountinfo record with the longest mount point that is a prefix of the resolved object's path, and, where several records share it, the last such record in file order.

advisories.title: The newly minted standing pin-rotation rule does not describe the ledger it was minted alongside
advisories.detail: The rule reads 'each successor retains the immediate predecessor round in appliesFindingsOf; earlier rounds recover via basedOn'. v6 did exactly that, retaining only the v5 round. v7 retains claude2v5, codexv5, claude2v6 and codexv6 — two rounds — so the artifact deviates from its own rule in the same edit that mints it.

advisories.suggestedFix: Either state that a successor retains at least the immediate predecessor round, or drop the v5 entries so the practice matches the rule.

advisories.title: Two named observation sources depend on a convention the contract does not state

detail.mountinfoOrdinal: 'fs_vfstype (mountinfo field 9)' matches the kernel documentation's numbering, in which field 7 is the variable-length optional-fields group and field 8 is the '-' separator. An implementer who splits the line on whitespace and indexes positionally lands on a different token whenever the number of optional fields is not one, which is common. The name and the ordinal disagree under the most obvious parsing strategy.
detail.osReleaseLocation: '/etc/os-release ID as published by os-release(5)' names one path while citing a specification that defines two, /etc/os-release with /usr/lib/os-release as fallback. On a host carrying only the /usr/lib copy, a reader following the path refuses (VERSION_ID unobtainable) and a reader following the specification produces a key.

advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: Both are narrow and both fail safe. The ID-absent case is already handled without a special rule, because os-release(5) supplies the default 'linux', which normalizes and falls to OTHER-PUBLISHER deterministically; and a host with no os-release file at all refuses through the existing VERSION_ID clause. I checked those before raising this and they are not defects.
advisories.suggestedFix: Cite the mountinfo token as the first field after the '-' separator rather than by ordinal, and say whether the os-release(5) /usr/lib fallback is in or out of scope.

repairVerification.status: REPAIRED — every element of both required repairs
repairVerification.detail: Checked against PTCB-V6-B1's requiredRepair element by element. Closed versioned tagged payload: schemeId opensip-linux-distro-userspace.1. Exact fields: publisher and userspaceRelease. Authoritative observation sources: /etc/os-release ID and VERSION_ID as published by os-release(5). Per-field normalization: publisher NFC + trim + ASCII case-fold, userspaceRelease NFC + trim with 'No case-fold' stated explicitly, which is the right asymmetry since VERSION_ID is case-significant in a way an ID is not. Unambiguous serialization: 'publisherToken + U+003A + userspaceRelease', with the delimiter named by code point. Equality: byte-exact after that serialization. The open alternative is not given its own tag but removed outright, which was Codex's other permitted branch — observation says 'No PLATFORM-ATTESTED platform-image alternate form' and notAdmitted says 'No second form. PLATFORM-ATTESTED platform-image identity is identityEvidence, not this selector.' My own additional element, the dangling normalization referent, is answered directly by canonicalIdentifier.normalizationReferent and by EXACT-BUILD.equality changing to 'after that scheme's named normalization'. The publisher vocabulary is genuinely closed rather than asserted closed: ten knownIds plus OTHER-PUBLISHER, whose 'when' fires on the normalized ID being absent from knownIds and whose token is 'other-' concatenated with a 64-hex SHA-256 of the normalized ID, so the function is total.
repairVerification.attacksRun: I tested the serialization for delimiter collision. publisherToken is colon-free by construction — every knownId is colon-free and the escape token is 'other-' plus hex — so a colon inside VERSION_ID cannot make two distinct field pairs serialize alike. I also tested the absent-ID and absent-file paths; see ADV-4, where they resolve.

Codex's ordering point is answered twice over, by normalizationBeforeEnumLookup: true and by lawfulOnlyWhen changing from 'the platform-reported filesystem type' to 'the normalized token is absent from identifierEnum', so EXT4 resolves to the enum member under every reader. Failure behaviour and record selection are the residue.

coordinatorNote: This is the strongest generation in the lineage and the first with no blockers. Both Codex blockers and my own are closed on their merits: the Linux scheme is now a real closed payload rather than prose calling itself closed, with a versioned schemeId, named sources, per-field normalization that is deliberately different between the two fields, a total publisher mapping, a code-point delimiter and an explicit resolution of the normalization referent I flagged as dangling; and the open platform-image form was removed rather than softened. The filesystem source correctly abandons f_fstypename on Linux — the concrete error I raised — and the enum-ordering point Codex caught and I missed is answered twice. sonameAbi is excluded from identity in four coordinated places using the exact vocabulary Codex required. The pin-rotation rule is now standing and ties back to the inherited line whose claim it supports. What keeps this at REJECT is one element of PTCB-V6-B2's required repair: failure behaviour was named in that repair and is still absent, and the Linux record-selection rule does not determine a unique mountinfo record under bind or overlay mounts, where more than one can carry the mount point. The artifact's own sibling field shows the standard — 'If VERSION_ID is absent the profile refuses' — so this is a gap of one clause rather than a design problem, and the four advisories are all small: a carried typing issue the artifact books honestly against itself, a rotation rule that over-retains relative to its own wording, a live-locator left pointing one block behind the one it marks LIVE, and two observation sources that rely on a parsing convention they do not state. I record one thing in my own favour and one against: the mountinfo ordinal is correct under the kernel documentation's numbering and I have graded it only as a convention risk rather than an error, and I did not catch the normalization-versus-enum ordering at v6 that Codex did. DR-126 stays OPEN. No per-OS table is populated, the single D-096 occurrence is a prohibition, and nothing here marks the row SATISFIED, qualifies G22, or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/. The subject, file 08, COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md and the review prompt were not edited and nothing was committed.
